You are planning a concrete implementation to make the "glint" coding-agent CLI produce dramatically better animated websites. Codebase: /home/lane/GR/glint-cli. Read AGENTS.md first (the contract), then these files fully: src/core/prompts.ts, src/core/agent.ts, src/core/tools.ts, src/core/config.ts, src/core/skills.ts, src/core/protocol.ts, src/core/compact.ts.

The model is fixed (groq/compound, text-only, no vision, no native function-calling — tools work via <glint:tool>{json}</glint:tool> text blocks). NO new models, NO new API keys. All improvements must be harness-side: system prompt, skills, the agent loop, and tools.

The planned improvements (already researched separately) are:
A) Inject a "frontend design" knowledge block — a slop-ban aesthetics rubric, an 8px spacing token system + modular type scale as CSS variables, a forced "DIRECTION" design-manifesto step, and canonical CDN snippets for GSAP/ScrollTrigger/Motion/anime.js + CSS scroll-driven-animation patterns.
B) A generate → rubric-scored self-critique → refine loop so the weak model iterates on its own frontend output against an explicit design rubric (Self-Refine pattern).
C) A static-analysis "design lint" the harness runs on generated HTML (no browser) that scans for deficiencies (hardcoded colors, ad-hoc font sizes, no scroll-reveal, no prefers-reduced-motion, no animation lib) and feeds text feedback into the loop.

Your job: map EXACTLY how to wire each of these into the existing architecture with minimal, idiomatic changes. For each, specify:
- Which file(s) change and where (function names, line ranges).
- Whether it should be a SKILL (src/core/skills.ts — note how skills are stored/loaded and whether a built-in/bundled skill mechanism exists or must be added), a system-prompt section (prompts.ts buildSystemPrompt), a new TOOL (tools.ts buildTools), or loop logic (agent.ts runTurn).
- How it stays inert for non-frontend tasks (must not bloat the prompt or fire the lint for a backend bug fix) — e.g. detection of frontend intent, or a tool the model opts into.
- How it respects existing constraints: the anti-fabrication guards, the reasoning-channel tool salvage + per-turn dedup, enabledTools:[], approval flow, effort/maxIterations budget, tsc-clean requirement, the "no UI imports in core" rule.

Key design question to resolve and recommend on: should the design knowledge live in the always-on system prompt (simple, but bloats every request) OR in a bundled skill that loads on demand OR be triggered by detecting frontend intent (html/css/website/landing-page keywords or generated-file extension)? Note: skills currently live in ~/.glint/skills and are user-created; there's no bundled-skill concept yet. Recommend the lowest-complexity path that keeps non-frontend tasks unaffected.

Deliver a step-by-step implementation plan with file-level specifics and the recommended architecture decision for each of A/B/C. This is a PLAN ONLY — do not edit any files. Be concrete enough that another engineer could implement it directly.

1	# AGENTS.md — Operating Rules for AI Agents in glint-cli
2	
3	glint is a free agent CLI by Glint Research: a Bun + TypeScript + Ink TUI that drives groq/compound through a text tool protocol. This file is the contract for any agent working in this repository. Read it fully before changing anything.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	bun install                  # install dependencies
9	bun run dev                  # run the TUI from source
10	bun run src/index.tsx -p "task" --yolo   # headless one-shot (the e2e test entry)
11	bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit       # type check — must stay clean
12	bun run build                # regenerate logo + compile dist/glint
13	bun run install-bin          # install dist/glint to ~/.local/bin
14	```
15	
16	All of these must keep working with no arguments and no manual setup. If your change affects any of them, rerun the affected one in the same session and prove it.
17	
18	## Architecture (read before editing)
19	
20	- `src/core/` — engine, no UI imports allowed here:
21	  - `groq.ts` streaming client (retries, SSE) · `protocol.ts` tool-block parsing (XML + sentinel forms)
22	  - `agent.ts` the loop: reasoning-channel salvage, turn-scoped dedup, reality/verification nudges
23	  - `tools.ts` tool registry · `prompts.ts` system prompt · `compact.ts` history compaction
24	  - `diagnostics.ts` hash-chained local JSONL traces · `logger.ts` file log · `session.ts`/`memory.ts`/`skills.ts` persistence
25	- `src/tui.tsx` + `src/components/` — Ink UI. Fullscreen alternate-screen layout: fixed `height={rows}` root, bottom-anchored transcript (`justifyContent="flex-end"` + `overflow="hidden"`), input + status welded to the bottom. No `<Static>`/native scrollback — PgUp/PgDn scrolls the in-app transcript. `startApp` enters/leaves the alt-screen buffer (`\x1b[?1049h/l`).
26	- `src/generated/logo.ts` — generated by `scripts/build-logo.ts` from `../embedme.html`. Never edit by hand.
27	- `src/headless.ts` — `-p` one-shot mode used for e2e testing.
28	
29	## Hard-won constraints (violate these and the agent breaks)
30	
31	1. **groq/compound has NO custom function calling.** Tools work via text blocks (`<glint:tool>{json}</glint:tool>`). The model drifts between formats — `protocol.ts` parses both XML and `<<<glint:tool` sentinel forms. Keep both.
32	2. **The model "executes" tools inside its reasoning channel.** `agent.ts` salvages calls from `res.reasoning`, deduped per turn (`turnExecuted`). Removing the dedup causes infinite re-execution loops; removing the salvage makes the agent claim work it never did.
33	3. **The model fabricates.** Three guards exist: the reality nudge (final answer claims actions, zero tools ran), the verification nudge (files modified, nothing run afterward), and premature-claim suppression (`claimsAction`). Test against fabrication explicitly after any prompt or loop change.
34	4. **Built-in compound tools must stay disabled in the agent loop** (`enabledTools: []`) or compound's server-side ReAct loop intercepts the conversation. Web access goes through the local `web_search` tool, which one-shots compound-mini WITH built-ins enabled.
35	5. **Non-zero bash exit must throw** (status: error) — silent failure re-enables fabricated success claims.
36	6. **The model leaks its base identity** ("I'm ChatGPT") and **describes files it never read**. The system prompt pins identity and bans assumption ("look first"); mid-round text longer than ~240 chars is held back as a draft answer. Keep both.
37	7. **Cost is computed from `usage_breakdown`** (compound is pass-through priced; `pricing.ts`). The streaming client must keep capturing `x_groq.usage_breakdown` from the final SSE chunk.
38	
39	## Rules
40	
41	- Real implementations only. No placeholders, no TODO stubs, no mock data presented as real.
42	- Type-check (`bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) must pass clean before declaring done.
43	- Every engine change gets an e2e proof: run a headless task that exercises it and verify the filesystem outcome independently — do not trust the agent's own claims (see constraint 3).
44	- TUI changes get a tmux proof: launch in tmux, send keys, capture-pane, read the render.
45	- Keep `src/core/` free of UI imports; keep UI free of direct Groq calls.
46	- The API key and model names in `config.ts` are hardcoded by explicit project requirement; env `GROQ_API_KEY` overrides. Do not "fix" this.
47	- Logging is mandatory: every new event type goes through `logger.ts`, every agent-visible event also through `diagnostics.trace`.
48	- Diagnostics are local-only by design ("the most secure transport is no transport"). Never add a network sink.
49	
50	## Final checklist
51	
52	1. tsc clean.
53	2. Headless e2e run (simple + one failure-mode task) with filesystem-verified results.
54	3. TUI smoke test in tmux if UI was touched.
55	4. `bun run build` succeeds and `dist/glint --version` works if anything under `src/` changed.
56	5. No placeholder text, no dead code, no claims without proof.
57

# Implementation Plan: Better Animated Websites in glint-cli

## Recommended architecture decision (the key question)

**Use a hybrid: a lazy-loaded, bundled "frontend design" knowledge block gated by frontend-intent detection, injected as ONE system-prompt section — NOT an always-on section and NOT the user-skill mechanism.**

Reasoning, ranked by the constraint "lowest complexity, non-frontend tasks unaffected":

- **Always-on system prompt** — rejected. The design block (rubric + tokens + CDN snippets + manifesto step) is 1.5–3 KB. Adding it to every request bloats a text-only model's prompt for backend bug fixes and violates the spirit of constraint 6 (keep the prompt lean so the model doesn't drift). Also pollutes subagents.
- **User-skill mechanism (`~/.glint/skills`)** — rejected as the primary path. Skills only inject `name + description` into the prompt (prompts.ts:107); the body only enters context when the user explicitly types `/name`. So a skill cannot passively influence "build me a landing page" unless the user knows to invoke it. There's no bundled-skill loader, and adding one is more code than a gated prompt section.
- **Frontend-intent-gated bundled section** — chosen. A pure string constant lives in a new core module; `buildSystemPrompt` appends it only when the turn's user message matches a frontend-intent regex. Zero new files in `~/.glint`, zero new tools required for A, inert for backend tasks by construction, never added for subagents.

The intent signal is computed in `runTurn` (it already has `userMessage`) and threaded into `buildSystemPrompt` via a new opt. This same boolean gates B and C, so all three share one detector.

---

## Shared foundation: frontend-intent detection

**New file: `src/core/frontend.ts`** (core module, no UI imports — compliant).

Exports:

```ts
export function isFrontendIntent(userMessage: string): boolean
```

- Regex over the user message for: `\b(website|web ?page|landing[ -]?page|html|css|tailwind|animat\w*|hero section|portfolio|microsite|scroll[- ]?(reveal|driven)|gsap|framer|marquee|parallax|svg)\b` plus file-extension hints `\.(html|css|svg)\b`.
- Keep it conservative (favor false-negative): a backend "fix the CSS parser bug in Rust" should ideally not trip it, but a stray match only costs one prompt section — acceptable. The lint (C) and refine loop (B) have their own stronger gates (actual generated `.html` files), so a false positive on intent alone does no harm beyond a few hundred tokens.

Also export the design knowledge constant and lint function from this same module (keeps all frontend concerns in one core file, satisfying "no UI in core" and giving `prompts.ts`/`agent.ts` a single import).

---

## A) Frontend design knowledge block

**Decision: system-prompt section, gated by `isFrontendIntent`.**

### Files & changes

1. **`src/core/frontend.ts` (new):** add
   ```ts
   export const FRONTEND_DESIGN_BLOCK: string
   ```
   A single template string containing:
   - **Slop-ban rubric** (prose, ~10 bullet "never do" rules: no centered-everything, no default system-font stacks without intent, no `#3498db`-era gradients, no unmotivated drop shadows, etc.).
   - **8px spacing scale + modular type scale as copy-paste CSS custom properties** (`:root { --space-1..--space-12; --step--1..--step-5; }`), with an instruction to *use the tokens, never ad-hoc px*.
   - **Forced "DIRECTION" step:** "Before writing any markup, output a 3–5 line DIRECTION manifesto (mood, palette with hex, type pairing, motion concept). Then build to it." This is the design-manifesto gate.
   - **Canonical CDN snippets:** exact `<script src=...>` tags for GSAP + ScrollTrigger, Motion One, anime.js, and a CSS `@scroll-timeline` / `animation-timeline: scroll()` reveal pattern, each with a one-line "when to use."
   - A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` requirement line.

2. **`src/core/prompts.ts:buildSystemPrompt`:**
   - Extend the opts type (line 25-29) with `frontend?: boolean`.
   - Import `FRONTEND_DESIGN_BLOCK` from `./frontend.ts` (line 8 area).
   - After the working-style push (line 103) and before `project`, add:
     ```ts
     if (!opts.subagent && opts.frontend) sections.push(FRONTEND_DESIGN_BLOCK);
     ```
   - Guarded by `!opts.subagent` so subagents never get it (matches the existing memory/skills/project pattern at 34-36).

3. **`src/core/agent.ts:runTurn`:**
   - At the top (after line 193), compute `const frontend = isFrontendIntent(userMessage);` (import from `./frontend.ts`).
   - Pass it at line 229: `buildSystemPrompt({ tools: effectiveTools, effort, frontend })`.
   - `trace("turn.frontend", { frontend })` for diagnostics (constraint: every agent-visible behavior change traced).

### Inertness & constraints

- Backend tasks: `frontend === false` → section absent → zero prompt bloat.
- Subagents (`runSubagent` builds its own prompt with `subagent: true`) get nothing — they never pass `frontend`, and the `!opts.subagent` guard double-protects.
- No new tool, no approval flow change, no `enabledTools` change. tsc-clean: only a new optional field and a string constant.
- Anti-fabrication guards untouched (this is pure prompt text).

---

## B) Generate → rubric-score → refine loop (Self-Refine)

**Decision: loop logic inside `agent.ts`, NOT a tool and NOT a skill.** It must fire automatically after the model produces frontend output, and it reuses the existing `chat` client the same way `reviewGoal` (agent.ts:145) already does. Making it a tool would require the weak model to *opt in*, which it won't reliably do.

### Where it hooks

The cleanest insertion point is the **terminal branch of `runTurn`** — the spot where `calls.length === 0` and all fabrication nudges have passed, right before `cb.onAssistantText?.(visible)` and `return` (agent.ts:342-349). At that moment the turn is "about to finish."

### Mechanism

1. **Gate (cheap, no extra LLM call unless warranted):** only run the refine loop if ALL hold:
   - `frontend === true` (from A's detector), AND
   - at least one `write_file`/`edit_file` produced an `.html`/`.css` file this turn (track during the tool-exec loop at agent.ts:378 — push the resolved path into a turn-scoped `producedFrontendFiles: string[]`), AND
   - a new config flag `refine` (see below) is enabled.

   This guarantees the loop never fires for a backend bug fix or a question — it requires real frontend files on disk.

2. **The loop** (new exported function in `agent.ts`, e.g. `refineFrontend(state, files, frontend, cb, signal)`), bounded by a small fixed cap (e.g. `maxRefineRounds = 2`, independent of `maxIterations` so it can't be starved by a high-effort budget — but each round still respects `signal`):
   - **Lint first (C):** run the static `designLint` (section C) on each produced file. Cheap, no LLM.
   - **Score (LLM critique):** one `chat` call to `effectiveModels().subagent` (compound-mini, cheap) with a *rubric-scored critic* system prompt: "You are a frontend design critic. Score this HTML/CSS against the rubric [embed the same rubric headings from `FRONTEND_DESIGN_BLOCK`]. Output `SCORE: n/10` then up to 5 concrete, actionable defects. If score ≥ 8 and no critical defects, output `PASS`." Pass the file contents (read from disk, capped) + the lint findings as the user message.
   - **Refine:** if not `PASS`, push a `user` message into `state.messages` of the form `[design review] Your page scored n/10. Fix these specific issues, then stop: <lint findings + critic defects>`, and **re-enter the normal round loop** (not a parallel loop) so all existing tool plumbing, approval flow, and fabrication guards apply unchanged. Simplest implementation: instead of a separate function, set a flag and `continue` the main `for` loop with an injected feedback message and a decremented refine budget — mirroring exactly how `reviewGoal` re-prompts via `queueRef` in the TUI, but kept inside `runTurn` so headless mode benefits too.

   Recommended concrete shape: add `let refineRounds = 0;` near the other counters (agent.ts:237-244). In the terminal branch, before returning:
   ```ts
   if (frontend && producedFrontendFiles.length && config.refine && refineRounds < 2) {
     const feedback = await scoreFrontend(producedFrontendFiles, signal); // lint + critic
     if (feedback) {           // null === PASS
       refineRounds++;
       state.messages.push({ role: "user", content: `[design review]\n${feedback}` });
       trace("turn.refine", { round: refineRounds });
       continue;              // re-enter loop; model fixes, writes again
     }
   }
   ```
   `scoreFrontend` lives in `frontend.ts` (lint) + a thin critic call in `agent.ts` (LLM), returning `null` on PASS.

3. **Config flag.** Add `refine: boolean` to `UserConfig` (config.ts:80-88) and `DEFAULTS` (config.ts:92-100), default `true` (it self-gates on frontend files, so it's safe on by default; can be exposed via a `/refine` toggle in `commands.ts` later). This makes the whole feature switchable without touching code.

### Inertness & constraints

- Fires only when real frontend files were written this turn → never on backend/question turns.
- Re-uses the main loop, so: approval flow intact (refined writes still prompt unless `--yolo`), `enabledTools: []` intact, reasoning-salvage + `turnExecuted` dedup intact (new feedback message is a normal `user` turn).
- **Anti-fabrication respected:** the critic runs on file contents *read from disk*, not on the model's claims — it cannot be fooled by a fabricated "I built it." The verify nudge (305) still independently applies.
- **Budget respected:** `refineRounds` capped at 2 and counts against nothing infinite; under `ultracode` (`maxIterations = Infinity`) the cap still bounds refine passes.
- tsc-clean: new function + one config field.
- Cost note (constraint 7): the critic uses compound-mini (`subagent` model) — cheap, and only on frontend turns.

---

## C) Static "design lint" (no browser)

**Decision: a pure function in `src/core/frontend.ts`, consumed by B's loop. NOT a standalone tool by default** (the weak model won't reliably call it), but **also expose it as an optional tool** so the model *can* self-check mid-build — low cost, high upside.

### Files & changes

1. **`src/core/frontend.ts`:** add
   ```ts
   export interface LintFinding { rule: string; detail: string }
   export function designLint(html: string): LintFinding[]
   ```
   Pure string/regex scan (no DOM, no browser, no deps). Rules:
   - **Hardcoded colors:** count raw `#[0-9a-f]{3,6}` / `rgb(`/`hsl(` occurrences that aren't inside a `:root`/`var(--…)` declaration → flag "uses N hardcoded colors; define a palette as CSS custom properties."
   - **Ad-hoc font sizes:** `font-size:\s*\d+px` not referencing `var(--step` → flag.
   - **No scroll reveal:** absence of any of `ScrollTrigger`, `animation-timeline`, `IntersectionObserver`, `data-scroll` → flag "no scroll-driven reveal."
   - **No `prefers-reduced-motion`:** absence of `prefers-reduced-motion` while animation is present → flag (accessibility).
   - **No animation lib / CSS animation:** absence of GSAP/Motion/anime CDN AND no `@keyframes`/`transition`/`animation-timeline` → flag "static page, no motion."
   - **Spacing tokens unused:** raw `margin:`/`padding:` with px and no `var(--space` → flag.

   Return `[]` (clean) when nothing trips. Each finding stringifies to one actionable line for the feedback message.

2. **B's loop** calls `designLint(readFileSync(file))` for each produced `.html`/`.css` file and concatenates findings into the critic input and the `[design review]` feedback.

3. **Optional opt-in tool** in `tools.ts:buildTools` (additive):
   ```ts
   add({
     name: "design_lint",
     description: "Statically check an HTML/CSS file for design/animation deficiencies (hardcoded colors, ad-hoc font sizes, missing scroll-reveal, missing prefers-reduced-motion, no animation). Returns a list of fixable issues.",
     args: `{"path": string}`,
     needsApproval: false,
     subagentSafe: true,
     run: async (args) => { /* read file, designLint, format findings */ },
   });
   ```
   - `needsApproval: false`, `subagentSafe: true` → harmless, read-only.
   - Its tool-doc line only appears in the prompt's `## Tools` list (always present), adding ~1 line. To keep it inert for backend turns we could gate it behind `frontend` in `buildTools`/`runTurn`'s `effectiveTools` filter, but the one-line cost is negligible; **recommend leaving it always-listed** for simplicity and because the model self-correcting on any HTML it touches is desirable. (If strict inertness is required, filter it out when `!frontend` in `runTurn` the same way auto-mode filters approval tools at agent.ts:224-226.)

### Inertness & constraints

- The lint function is pure and only invoked by B (gated on frontend files) or by explicit tool call → never runs for a backend bug fix.
- No browser, no network (honors "no network sink" / local-only).
- `executeTool` already wraps errors; file-not-found throws → surfaces as a normal tool error.
- tsc-clean: pure functions + one tool registration.
